official_documentation.finding: The main header is 100 bytes; its leading 16 bytes identify SQLite format 3. A valid signature is necessary but does not prove page/schema/journal/WAL validity. Hot sidecars are part of database state.
Normal read access may first replay and finalize a hot rollback journal. A nonempty sidecar alone is not evidence of a valid recoverable journal.
WAL is persistent database state. Read-only connection modes can still require existing or creatable WAL/shared-memory files; read-only is not a general no-side-effect guarantee.
Immutable asserts that the underlying file will not change and disables locks/change detection. It must not be used as the authority for a live WAL snapshot.

sections: 2.2 Posix advisory locks canceled by close
official_documentation.finding: A raw open/read/close of even the first 16 bytes can release other same-process POSIX locks. SQLite 3.51 protections are explicitly not a universal cure; SQLite-managed descriptors share VFS bookkeeping.

static_findings.finding: On reopening a zero-page main, pagerOpenWalIfPresent can delete an existing -wal without first accepting its frames. hasHotJournal can also delete an unopened -journal for a zero-page main.
static_findings.application_inference: Missing/zero main with nonempty retained sidecars must not be admitted merely because a sidecar exists. Preserve the combination and return a dedicated-recovery/refusal outcome. This does not prove every such sidecar is valueless, nor authorize deleting it.

static_findings.finding: Btree header checks include magic, read/write version, payload fractions, page-size/usable-size and page-count constraints after acquiring the pager's page-one view.
static_findings.application_inference: A main-only immutable header probe is stronger than checking 16 raw bytes, but is not current WAL schema or whole-database acceptance. Recoverable damaged-main/hot-sidecar combinations can be conservatively refused without being declared irrecoverable.

static_findings.finding: user_version is HEADER_VALUE with NoColumns1 Result0 and no NeedSchema flag. Its read branch generates OP_Transaction P2=0, OP_ReadCookie and ResultRow; ReadCookie obtains Btree metadata from page one. The core open path delays schema loading. Compiled-in and registered automatic extension hooks remain caveats.
static_findings.application_inference: Use only PRAGMA user_version without assignment as an ignored header-read result; do not infer current application version/migration state from it. Actual wrapper/compile/runtime behavior requires containing-H Actions.

static_findings.finding: The normal VFS main-file open happens before immutable is interpreted. Immutable sets pager noLock/tempFile/reader state; this normal header-only connection does not open or recover the WAL/rollback journal. Close delegates to SQLite VFS; an unopened pWal/jfd does not initiate sidecar cleanup.
static_findings.limits: This applies to the independent read-only header-probe path, not arbitrary extensions, writes, custom VFS or shared cache reuse.

static_findings.finding: MAIN_DB is not assigned UNIXFILE_NOLOCK by unixOpen merely because immutable was requested. Under POSIX io methods, fillInUnixFile registers dev/inode via findInodeInfo. unixClose checks shared inode nLock; if nonzero it stores the descriptor in pending-FD state and sets current h=-1, preventing immediate close until locks are released.
static_findings.application_inference: A private-cache immutable connection using the same bundled SQLite and default POSIX VFS avoids the normal raw-FD-close lock loss. This protects descriptor lifetime, not a consistent concurrent main-file snapshot.

static_findings.finding: unix-none selects nolockIoMethods, whose nolockClose directly closes the file without the POSIX inode/pending-FD close deferral.
static_findings.application_inference: Do not add vfs=unix-none/custom no-lock VFS to the replacement. Pager.noLock under immutable and a true no-lock VFS are distinct layers.

limitations: No local SQLite execution, build, test, formatter, generator or validator was run.
No root repository production code, schema, workflow, ledger or acceptance state was changed by this research.
Only selected exact-release source ranges were semantically reviewed; full-file reading/acceptance is not claimed.
Header probe success is not current WAL/rollback state, schema validation, integrity of all pages, or a migration-version result.
Immutable reads can observe a changing main file; conservatively refusing is different from authorizing changes. Metadata-to-open and sidecar-observation races remain.

POSIX descriptor proof assumes the same SQLite instance/inode registry and compatible default VFS. Different linked SQLite copies, custom VFS, manual descriptors and path replacement are outside the proof.
macOS automatic filesystem VFS selection may choose non-POSIX methods. This review does not grant coverage to unix-none/WebDAV/other custom methods.
findInodeInfo's fstat-error path may immediately close the descriptor; the normal successful-open proof does not promise safety under all OS faults.
SQLITE_OPEN_PRIVATE_CACHE avoids sharing the probe pager with an existing live connection. No automatic-extension behavior or nonstandard compile flag is accepted by this static review.
Containing-H GitHub Actions must execute preserved unknown/corrupt-byte negatives, genuine retained-WAL positive recovery and a meaningful same-process POSIX writer-lock preservation control.

finding.basis: Source-proven reachability of an uncoordinated raw File close on a SQLite main-file inode while another same-process SQLite connection can be alive. The POSIX-close hazard was supplied by the parent from SQLite's official howtocorrupt section 2.2; separate reviewers own documentation/version/VFS qualification. This receipt does not claim runtime lock loss.
single_workers_schedule: A valid retained Human store exists after Host restart and the Workers owner cache is empty.
Request A enters createHumanConversation, acquires its per-conversation mutation lock, observes cached_owner=None at production.rs:2736-2740, and releases the owner-map mutex.
Request B enters a Human transcript/tail/list reader on a different Gateway connection; it does not take the mutation lock and opens/registers a SQLite owner through production.rs:2859-2899.

A resumes its already-selected None branch at 2749, calls agent_db.rs:263, and opens/reads/closes the main file through std::fs::File while B's SQLite owner remains alive; B's read operation can overlap this interval.
The later owner-map entry merge at 2790-2792 preserves B's Arc but cannot undo or prevent the earlier raw close.
distinct_workers_schedule: W1 and W2 have the same agents_root and Human identity but independent owner/lock maps.
W1 opens the canonical Human store and retains its SQLite candidate or cached owner.
W2 has no cached owner and enters the same raw probe despite W1's positive live count.
The existing distinct_worker_creators test source at 527-543 explicitly constructs this ownership overlap; it does not measure OS locks.
safe_cases_that_do_not_close_the_gap: A create call that finds an existing cached owner reuses it without invoking the probe.
Two create calls for the same pair in the same Workers instance are serialized by human_message_lock.
Neither fact serializes read-side opens nor independent Workers.
count_gate_limitations: The current probe runs before any live count check and ignores positive counts.
Count, open, registration, and close are separate operations rather than one process-wide admission interval.
SQLite opens before registration and count release precedes actual SQLite close.
PathBuf identity does not establish inode identity for aliases.
Direct SQLite/projection/maintenance connections are not all represented in this owner count.
finding.minimal_required_fix_boundary: Preserve NOTADB, short-header, retained-sidecar and metadata fail-closed behavior while replacing the uncoordinated raw main-file open/read/close with a SQLite-coordinated mechanism. A one-time count==0 check, per-Workers mutex alone, or merely reordering the WAL check is not a demonstrated fix.
missing_behavior_oracles: A same-process SQLite owner holds a real transaction/lock while a second Human opener traverses the header path; an independent process must still be unable to obtain the conflicting lock before and after the probe.
The original transaction must remain usable and committed data/metadata/main-file/sidecar preservation must be checked.
A deterministic cold-cache single-Workers create/read interleaving must cover the gap between cached None lookup and probe.
These are requested verification boundaries, not authored or executed tests in this receipt.
